hints.title: Postorder Traversal
hints.text: A subtree can only be verified as valid if its left and right subtrees are valid.

hints.title: Subtree Return Tuple
hints.text: Return four values from each subtree: whether it is a valid ordered subtree, its total sum, its minimum key, and its maximum key.

hints.title: Boundary Comparison
hints.text: For the current node to form a valid ordered structure, node.val must exceed left_max and be less than right_min.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxSumBST(self, root) -> int:
        self.max_sum = 0
        def dfs(node):
            if not node:
                return True, float("inf"), float("-inf"), 0
            l_valid, l_min, l_max, l_sum = dfs(node.left)
            r_valid, r_min, r_max, r_sum = dfs(node.right)
            if l_valid and r_valid and l_max < node.val < r_min:
                total = l_sum + r_sum + node.val
                self.max_sum = max(self.max_sum, total)
                return True, min(l_min, node.val), max(r_max, node.val), total
            return False, 0, 0, 0
        dfs(root)
        return self.max_sum
```

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Validating each subtree separately using top-down checks yields quadratic O(N^2) time on skewed trees.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bottom-up postorder gathers validation status, bounds, and sum in O(1) per node.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate utilizes a postorder tuple returning (is_valid, min_val, max_val, sum).
complexity.notes: Maximum sum could be 0 if all values are negative.
